The fork() system call is used to create a new process by duplicating the calling (parent) process. It returns 0 to the child process and PID of the child to the parent process, allowing both processes to run independently.

lq.q: Explain how process creation is done using fork() in Unix/Linux systems. Describe the role of getpid() , getppid() , and wait() functions with examples.
answer: In Unix/Linux operating systems, a new process is created using the fork() system call. It duplicates the calling process and creates a child process , which runs independently but initially shares the same memory space.
